meta.name: Organize Gmail inbox labels with Jev TypeSafe AI (System One)

name: Intelligent Email Organization with Jev (TypeSafe AI) for Gmail

parameters.content:
## Intelligent Email Organization with Jev for Gmail

### How it works

1. A schedule trigger searches Gmail every five minutes for messages that carry no user label yet.
2. Each message is sent to Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, which returns one label from a fixed set plus a calibrated confidence, as a typed answer rather than text to parse.
3. Code turns that judgment into a decision: file it when confident, escalate to Action Required when the category is unclear but the mail clearly needs a reply, otherwise park it in Needs Review rather than guess.
4. Any label the run needs but Gmail does not have yet is created once, deduplicated, before a single label id is read.
5. Labels are applied and the workflow loops back to the search, draining the backlog 50 emails at a time.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create a Bearer Auth credential holding your TypeSafe API key and select it on Classify Email with Jev.
- [ ] Select your Gmail OAuth2 credential on the four Gmail nodes.
- [ ] Run once manually with the trigger disabled, then read Decide Label from Confidence to see each verdict and its confidence.
- [ ] Tune CONFIDENCE FLOOR and NEEDS REPLY FLOOR at the top of that node against your own mail before enabling the schedule.

### Customization

Edit the criteria map in Classify Email with Jev to change the label taxonomy; every other node follows automatically. Raise MAX ROUNDS in Check for Next Batch to clear a larger backlog in one execution.

## Fetch unlabelled emails

Searches Gmail every five minutes for messages that carry no user label, 50 per round.

## Classify and decide

Jev returns a typed label and a calibrated confidence; code turns that into one label name.

## Create missing labels once

Diffs the needed names against Gmail and creates each new label exactly once, before any id is read.

## Apply labels and loop

Attaches fresh label ids, applies them, then loops back until the backlog is drained.

nodes.name: Fetch Unlabelled Emails
nodes.notes: has:nouserlabels replaces the hardcoded Label_* exclusion list, so this is not tied to one account.

nodes.name: Classify Email with Jev
nodes.notes:
Both questions ride one request and are evaluated in parallel, so needs_reply costs almost nothing.
retryOnFail covers 429 / 529; onError keeps one bad email from killing the batch (it falls through to Needs Review).

nodes.name: Decide Label from Confidence
nodes.notes: Jev supplies judgment; this node decides. Names only - no Gmail ids yet.

nodes.name: List Gmail Labels
nodes.notes: executeOnce: one label list per run, not one per email.

nodes.name: Find Missing Labels
nodes.notes: Deduplicates. This is the node that fixes 'Label name exists or conflicts'.

nodes.name: Create Gmail Label
nodes.notes: At most one call per distinct new name. Continue-on-error tolerates a name Gmail refuses; those emails fall back to Needs Review.

nodes.name: Reload Gmail Labels
nodes.notes: Re-read AFTER creation so newly made labels have ids. Both branches converge here.

nodes.name: Resolve Label Ids
nodes.notes: Joins fresh label ids back onto each email decision.

nodes.name: Apply Label to Email
nodes.notes: Plain field reads - no cross-node item pairing needed any more.

nodes.name: Check for Next Batch
nodes.notes:
Loops back to the Gmail search until the backlog is drained.
Stops on: nothing labelled, a partial page, or the round ceiling.
